claim: Adding every experience without a quality filter hurts LLM agents versus a small fixed memory (RegAgent 55.48 vs 67.53; EHRAgent 13.05 vs 16.75; AgentDriver 32.32 vs 40.11; CIC-IoT 59.90 vs 71.50, GPT-4o-mini). Errors propagate because outputs copy the outputs of similar retrieved cases.
agent_test: Same agent, same tokens: add-all vs fixed-size vs add-if-verified over a stream of 2000+ tasks.

claim: A strict (accurate) retain gate beats both add-all and fixed memory: strict 70.95/38.50/51.00/85.40 vs add-all 55.48/13.05/32.32/59.90. Coarse judges (C1) can fall below the fixed baseline (RegAgent 63.18 vs 67.53).
agent_test: Vary judge accuracy (ground truth, strong LLM, weak LLM) for the retain decision at equal token budget.
note_gap_search: Judge-quality effect now seen in a second system (Memory-R1: manager quality moves F1 by 6-8 points). Pan et al. show 75-90% accurate judges already help web agents.

claim: Judge accuracy matters, but sensitivity is disputed: ReasoningBank judge was 72.7% accurate and simulated accuracy from 100% to 50% moved success only in a narrow band (about 47.6 to 53), while Xiong coarse judges lose 4 to 12 points against a strict one.
agent_test: Simulate noisy retain judges at 100/80/60% accuracy on one benchmark; see which paper's sensitivity holds.
note_gap_search: Still contested. Pan et al. (judges 74-93% accurate, large gains) side with ReasoningBank for outcome-checkable web tasks; Huang et al. suggest same-model judging of reasoning is unreliable. Likely rule: gate on outcome or verifier where one exists.

claim: Deleting cases by past utility (history-based) with a strict judge can raise accuracy while shrinking memory: EHRAgent 38.67->42.06 (1012->784), CIC-IoT 85.40->89.60 (904->788); mixed on RegAgent (70.95->69.80) and AgentDriver (+0.8).
agent_test: Track per-case use and downstream outcome; delete low-utility cases; compare to no deletion at equal tokens.

claim: Aggressive periodic pruning shrinks memory 60-90% at roughly flat accuracy under a strict judge (EHRAgent 1012->302, 38.67->38.59; AgentDriver 1178->467, 51.00->50.94) but costs more on RegAgent (-3.3) and CIC-IoT (-4.6).
agent_test: Sweep memory cap; plot accuracy vs size to find the knee.

claim: Performance converges as a memory cap grows (caps of 100-180 records near unbounded results), so unbounded retention is not needed.
agent_test: Cap sweep at 50/100/200/unbounded.
note_gap_search: ACE pruning trigger at 10K vs 100K tokens on FiNER gives 78.6 vs 78.3 (flat). Memp: too many retrieved memories lowers performance.

claim: Footprint/competence-based deletion keeps 100% competence on a 50-case property base (160 targets, limit 75) while random reaches 86% and utility-only 80%; minimal competent base is 27 cases (20 pivotal, 5 auxiliary, 25 support in 7 groups).
agent_test: Port to an LLM case bank: coverage = tasks a case helps solve; delete auxiliary/support first, pivotal last. Assumes case distribution approximates target distribution. Original not re-opened by cross-checker.

claim: Greedy competence-based case addition covers at least 63% of optimal coverage (set-cover reduction, NP-complete); about 15% of cases give about 50% of coverage and 50% of cases give about 85%.
agent_test: Measure the coverage curve of an LLM case bank; check whether a small core carries most gains.

claim: For instance-based learners, the best reduction method (DROP3) keeps about 14% of storage with about 1 point loss (81.14 vs kNN 82.11) and beats kNN under noise (80.00 vs 78.93); naive condensation (CNN, IB2) collapses on noise (68.14, 67.80).
agent_test: Noise-robust pruning: test dedupe/prune on a case bank seeded with 20% wrong cases. Figures not re-verified (PDF not found).
note_gap_search: Noise handling for LLM banks: wrong labels hurt generation heavily (Gao) but barely hurt classification (Min).

claim: Curated or synthesized memory beats raw full-history appending: Claude 3.5 Sonnet AIME 2024 full-history 26.7 vs curated 50.0; GPT-4o full-history 6.7 vs baseline 20.0 vs DC-RS 40.0. AIME 2024 has 30 questions (1 item = 3.3 points).
agent_test: Compare raw transcript, retrieval-only and curated cheatsheet at equal context tokens, with 100+ items.

claim: Curation gains are model dependent and may be noise: GPT-4o GPQA-Diamond flat (57.1 to 57.1 in the table; text says 58.1); Haiku gains mixed; retrieval can confuse.
agent_test: Run curation on weak and strong backbones; report confidence intervals.
note_gap_search: Evo-Memory (Gemini, Claude 3.7) also shows only moderate single-turn gains and a strong raw-retrieval baseline.

claim: Experience reuse works through retrieval plus abstracted insights: ExpeL full 39.0 vs ReAct 28.0 (HotpotQA); ALFWorld task-similarity retrieval 59.0 vs random 42.5, reasoning similarity 48.5, ReAct 40.0. Insights-only and retrieve-only are each below full.
agent_test: Ablate retrieval ranker and insight layer at equal tokens.
note_gap_search: Memp (three backbones) agrees: reflexion-style in-place revision beats append and success-only.

claim: Insight stores with ADD/EDIT/UPVOTE/DOWNVOTE (importance count, removal at 0) outperform hand-crafted insights, but the vote-based pruning itself was not ablated.
agent_test: Ablate vote-based pruning vs append-only insights.

claim: Rewriting a growing context wholesale can collapse it (ACE on AppWorld: 18,282 tokens at 66.7 accuracy, then 122 tokens at 57.1, below the 63.7 baseline), which motivates incremental delta updates.
agent_test: Compare delta updates against full rewrite of the notes file.

claim: Failures help memory: ReasoningBank with failures 49.7 vs success-only 46.5 (WebArena Shopping, Gemini-2.5-flash); overall gains +8.3/+7.2/+4.6 over three backbones; AWM-style success-only memory dropped when failures were added (44.4 to 42.2).
agent_test: Store failure lessons vs success-only at equal tokens.
note_gap_search: Evo-Memory: unfiltered failures degrade baselines but a refining method stays robust. Memp discards failures in its validation arm and revises in place in its best arm. Share of failures to keep is still untested.

claim: Self-generated trajectories with outcome-weighted curation improve over a fixed database: ALFWorld 0.73->0.89 (Traj-Bootstrap), 0.93 with exemplar curation; Wordcraft 0.55->0.72 exemplar-level; database-level curation gives small or no gain.
agent_test: Score each stored case by retrieval-weighted outcome; prune by score.

claim: Case-bank size saturates quickly: Memento K=4 neighbours F1 64.5 vs K=0 59.9; K=8 to 32 no better; no learning-curve drops over about 3k items, so swamping was not seen at that size.
agent_test: Check swamping at 10x larger bank; add-only may be fine while the bank stays small.
note_gap_search: Speed is not the limit: A-Mem retrieval time 0.31 us at 1k to 3.70 us at 1M notes; Weller best-case limit is 500k+ docs. No accuracy-vs-bank-size curve beyond 3k exists yet.

claim: Workflow induction quality matters little: rule-based vs LM-based induction differ by 0.1 on WebArena; offline vs online induction trade places by split (cross-domain 32.6 vs 35.5).
agent_test: Cheap rule-based vs LLM-based case abstraction at equal tokens.

claim: Memory systems trade accuracy for cost: Mem0 about 67% judge score vs full context about 73%, with p95 latency 1.44 s vs about 17 s and over 90% fewer tokens; full context stays most accurate.
agent_test: Report accuracy per token for any pruning policy.
note_gap_search: ACE: dedup/merge by non-LLM similarity is credited with cost and latency saving (82.3% fewer rollouts on AppWorld offline adaptation); accuracy effect of dedup threshold is within noise.

claim: The utility problem (retaining more can slow or hurt) is the founding framing of maintenance (Minton 1990; Francis and Ram 1993); the LLM add-all < fixed result is a modern reappearance, but the originals were not read.
agent_test: Original numbers unverified; cite only as framing.
note_gap_search: Minton read second-hand (review plus author reply): about 20% of rules kept, 2-3x speed-ups, utility = savings minus cost. Francis and Ram 1993 still unread (reference only).

claim: Competence-model update is cheap: updating a footprint model takes about 20% of comparisons at 1400 cases (5x speed-up) with 99.6% accuracy at k=3.
agent_test: Only relevant if banks reach thousands of cases.

claim: Ebbinghaus-style forgetting (MemoryBank) has no ablation against no forgetting, so its value is untested.
agent_test: Test decay forgetting vs utility-based deletion.
note_gap_search: Re-checked MemoryBank, SAGE and MemoryOS. None ablates decay or heat eviction against recency or no forgetting.

claim: Generative agents: removing reflection lowers TrueSkill from 29.89 to 26.88; no memory, planning or reflection gives 21.21 (N=100 raters).
agent_test: Reflection-layer ablation only, not a maintenance claim.

claim: Retrieve-all raw experience is a hard baseline on non-agentic reasoning: in Evo-Memory (AIME, GPQA, MMLU-Pro, ToolBench; Gemini 2.5 and Claude 3.7) ExpRAG is about equal to the best evolving method on single-turn sets (Gemini Flash average 0.65 for ReMem), gains are moderate, and gain tracks task similarity (r 0.56-0.72).
agent_test: Run a pruning rule against plain top-k retrieval of all cases at equal k on AIME/GPQA.

claim: Wrong labels in a demonstration pool hurt generation tasks a lot (SciQ at 60% noise: TopK 29.31 EM, 48.06 after local-perplexity cleaning) but barely hurt classification (random labels cost 0-5%, avg 2.6%).
agent_test: Test a local neighbour-consistency edit on a bank with injected wrong answers, for reasoning vs classification tasks.

claim: Selection quality matters less as the number of in-context cases grows: BM25 retrieval gain over random falls from 51.5 points (1-shot) to 4.9 (1500-shot) on Banking-77; cheaper cached random sets compete.
agent_test: Compare per-query retrieval with a cached fixed set at equal tokens.

claim: Embedding-based coverage can be defined for LLM banks, but only at query time so far: set-level BERTScore-Recall coverage beats independent similarity ranking by up to 17 points on compositional tasks; diversity-based pool selection (vote-k) beats random by 11-13% relative. No study applies it to delete cases.
agent_test: Define a case as pivotal if removing it drops coverage of a held-out query set; test deletion against random.

claim: Updating neighbouring notes at insert time (memory evolution) improves answers more than plain append, without deletion: A-Mem multi-hop F1 27.02 vs 21.35 without evolution.
agent_test: Compare append, merge-with-neighbour and delete on the same stream.

claim: Dedup threshold and pruning trigger have flat effects on accuracy on a non-agentic task (FiNER): dedup 50/70/90% gives 77.0/73.9/78.6; pruning trigger 10K/50K/100K tokens gives 78.6/78.4/78.3. There is no clean on/off dedup test.
agent_test: Run dedup on vs off with several seeds at equal tokens.

claim: Usage-based or heat-based eviction (MemoryOS) and Ebbinghaus decay (MemoryBank, SAGE) are in use but none of the three papers compares them with recency or no forgetting; SAGE only compares memory vs no memory.
agent_test: Head-to-head: recency, usage, decay, no deletion at a fixed cap.
